datasets_evaluated.evidence: Experiments on a mixed dataset which is constructed by CICIDS2017 and other ransomware datasets show comparing with other deep learning network, such as AlexNet, ResNet and DenseNet etc.

label_source.evidence: Ransomware traffic is collected from the following three websites: Malware-Traffic-Analysis.net [26], PacketTotal [27] and Interactive Online Malware Analysis Sandbox [28].

label_feature_overlap.evidence: Deep learning classifier usually uses two-dimensional image as input, and automatically extracts the non-linear feature to achieve end-to-end classification.

features_used.evidence: Network traffic is essentially a sequence of byte. One byte is a two-digit hexadecimal number and the range of corresponding decimal value is 0-255, which is exactly the interval of pixel gray value.

feature_groups.evidence: By arranging from top to bottom, left to right, a session can be converted from a sequence to a two-dimensional image.

cert_fields_read.evidence: In order to avoid excessive impact coming from IP address, port information and SNI (Server Name Indication) when training the classification model (since the detection model may rely too much on these information), the above information in a session is further filtered.

tls_versions_stated.evidence: There are seven classes of ransomware encrypted by TLSv1.0 or TLSv1.2: cerber, cryptowall, gandcrab, locky, shade, teslacrypt, and wannacry.

model_family.evidence: In this framework, DCGAN (Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network) is adopted to train a generator which has good performance to generate adversarial sample, and is transferred to the generator of TGAN.
